decisive_items: Hebreden node at DIP of the left index finger of the case
Small red node and mild joint deformity at distal interphalangeal joint of left index finger
response.rationale: The presence of a Heberden node at the DIP joint is pathognomonic for osteoarthritis, supported by negative inflammatory markers and absence of RF/anti-CCP, ruling out inflammatory arthritis.

rejected.why: Negative RF and anti-CCP, and Heberden node are not typical of RA.
No clear reactive trigger; Heberden node and DIP involvement favor OA.
Back pain is nonspecific; Heberden node and DIP involvement are more consistent with OA.
No direct evidence linking SARS-CoV-2 to arthritis; Heberden node is a degenerative finding.
Temporal association with vaccination is insufficient; Heberden node and DIP involvement are classic for OA.
